answer: Grant one credential per human through a grove of issuers - registries, universities, co-ops - not one authority. An applicant proves personhood to any k of n issuers; each returns a blinded partial credential, and k parts combined unlock one registration tied to a nullifier blocking reuse. No single karst channel controls issuance: faking one identity means fooling or bribing k issuers, so cost grows k-fold per fake, and a crystal-clear count per issuer exposes over-minting. Limits: threshold collusion, regions lacking an issuer - rotate issuers, cap credentials, slash over-issuers.
